steps.title: Draw a Card
text: Start your turn by drawing 1 card from the top of your deck. If your deck is empty, you lose the game.
Draw 1 card from the top of your deck and add it to your hand.
If you cannot draw because your deck is empty at the beginning of your turn, you lose the game. The player going first still draws a card on their first turn.

steps.title: Action Phase
text: Perform any of the following actions in any order, as many times as each allows.

steps.title: A) Put Basic Pokemon on Your Bench
text: Choose any number of Basic Pokemon from your hand and place them face up on your Bench. Your Bench can hold up to 5 Pokemon at a time.

steps.title: B) Evolve Pokemon
text: If you have a Pokemon in your hand that says "Evolves from [Name]" and [Name] is a Pokemon you have had in play since the start of your turn, you may play that card on top of it.
You can evolve Basic to Stage 1, or Stage 1 to Stage 2. A Pokemon cannot evolve on its first turn in play. Neither player can evolve on their very first turn of the game.
When a Pokemon evolves, it keeps all attached cards and damage counters, but loses all Special Conditions and other effects.

steps.title: C) Attach an Energy Card
text: Take 1 Energy card from your hand and attach it to one of your Pokemon (Active or Benched). You can only do this once per turn.

steps.title: D) Play Trainer Cards
bullets: **Item cards** — Play as many as you want per turn. Do what the card says, then discard it.
**Supporter cards** — Play only 1 per turn. The player going first cannot play a Supporter on their first turn.
**Stadium cards** — Play only 1 per turn. Stays in play with ongoing effects. Only 1 Stadium can be in play at a time — playing a new one discards the old one.
**Pokemon Tool cards** — Attach to 1 of your Pokemon (max 1 Tool per Pokemon). Stays attached until removed.

steps.title: E) Retreat Your Active Pokemon
text: Discard Energy from your Active Pokemon equal to its Retreat Cost (printed bottom-right). Then switch it with a Benched Pokemon. You can only retreat once per turn.
Asleep and Paralyzed Pokemon cannot retreat. When your Active Pokemon moves to the Bench, it recovers from all Special Conditions and attack effects.

steps.title: F) Use Abilities
text: Many Pokemon have Abilities you can use during your turn. Abilities are not attacks — using one does not end your turn. You can use Abilities from both Active and Benched Pokemon.

steps.title: Attack
text: Choose an attack on your Active Pokemon, verify you have the required Energy, and declare your attack. Your turn ends afterward.
The player going first cannot attack on their first turn.

steps.title: Attack Steps
text: After attacking, check if any Pokemon were Knocked Out. For each KO, the opponent takes Prize card(s) and promotes a new Active Pokemon from their Bench.
bullets: **1. Check Energy** — Ensure your Active Pokemon has the required Energy attached. Colorless symbols mean any type works. Attacks with cost 0 need no Energy.
**2. Check Weakness & Resistance** — If the defending Pokemon has Weakness to your type (e.g. x2), double the damage. If it has Resistance (e.g. -20), subtract that. Don't apply to Benched Pokemon.
**3. Place Damage Counters** — Place 1 damage counter (10 HP) for each 10 damage dealt, after modifiers. If a Pokemon's total damage equals or exceeds its HP, it's Knocked Out.

steps.title: Pokemon Checkup
text: Between turns, resolve Special Conditions and any between-turn effects.
After your turn ends, resolve Pokemon Checkup in this order:
Apply any effects from Abilities or Trainer cards that specify they happen during Pokemon Checkup.
After both players complete checks, any Pokemon reduced to 0 HP is Knocked Out and the opponent takes a Prize card. Then the next turn begins.
bullets: **1. Poisoned** — Place 1 damage counter on the Poisoned Pokemon.
**2. Burned** — Place 2 damage counters, then flip a coin. Heads recovers the Pokemon.
**3. Asleep** — Flip a coin. Heads recovers; tails stays Asleep.
**4. Paralyzed** — Recovers automatically if Paralyzed since the end of its owner's last turn.
